text:
Brock Nelson is the most normal player on a strange Avalanche team. Five goals, 11 points, finishing exactly at his expected goals, and Colorado holds 55% of the chances at five on five when he's out there.

The quiet part is the last ten games: four points, and his ice time down more than two minutes a night. It doesn't look like a decline so much as a shuffle. Evolving-Hockey had him as one of the best play drivers in the league last season, 98th percentile among forwards for the chances his team created with him on, and better than his goals said (4.1 expected wins against 2.0 actual). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile for chances from the slot.

He scored 33 goals last season and has more than 1,000 games behind him. His goals have come at good moments: by our win probability, they've added more than his chances would predict. Our range for the season: 42 to 62 points.
